title: Prune redundant route heuristics and modernize fallback state
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Over time the smart routing layer accrued several overlapping heuristics and incremental fallback flags to handle regional quirks, capacity spikes, and model-variant compatibility. This has increased maintenance cost, caused non-deterministic fallback ordering, and added ~6-12ms median extra decision latency in the hot path for high-throughput customers.

Goal: Reduce cognitive and runtime overhead by pruning redundant heuristics, collapsing legacy per-region overrides into a single prioritized rule-set, and replacing the ad-hoc fallback flags with a small, testable fallback state machine. Deliver a refactor that is feature-equivalent (no customer-visible behavior change at steady state), improves median routing latency by >=10%, and reduces code paths touching policy evaluation by ~30%.

Scope:
- Audit and remove heuristics that were introduced as hotfixes between 2022-2024 and have been superseded by newer policies.
- Introduce a deterministic fallback state machine (Idle -> CandidateSelection -> FallbackPrepare -> Commit -> Emit) with clear transition rules and timeouts.
- Consolidate regional overrides into "region-affinity" metadata consumed by the state machine instead of scattered if/else branches.
- Update policy-engine client to v1.2.0 (backwards-compatible API) and adapt scoring hook calls.
- Add unit + integration tests that simulate regional failures, capacity constraints, and multi-tenant routing.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI test coverage for the fallback state machine >= 85% for affected modules.
- PR benchmark shows median routing decision latency reduced by >=10% on our perf harness (p99 must not regress more than 5%).
- No customer-facing behavior regression in canary run across two regions (us-west, eu-central) for 48h.
- Code review approvals from runtime and infra owners.

Rollout plan: branch -> feature-flag behind "routing_v2" -> internal canary (small percentage) -> region canaries -> full rollout with automatic rollback on error rate or latency SLO violation.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle ordering changes cause different fallback model variants to be selected under rare capacity pressure. Mitigation: keep a compatibility shim that can replay legacy ordering for specific customers and add an A/B evaluation harness.
- Risk: policy-engine upgrade surfaces transient scoring differences. Mitigation: run dual scoring in canary to compare outputs for a sample of requests before switching consumers.

Notes: primary repo patch is tracked in the PRs below; design doc in Confluence links high-level state transitions and examples of corner cases.

2025-03-28: Opened primary PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345 with the state machine and removal of 4 legacy heuristics. Marked as WIP, requested reviews from @sophia and @diego.
